parts:
Hi everybody,

I am trying to implement my own function in C++ and expose it to STAN just as it is described here:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Contributing-New-Functions-to-Stan

(The function is intended for private use only, I do not intend to test or submit it to stan git project.)
To start with something simple, I just want to copy the function 'abs' (only for the unary, not vector-valued arguments)
and name it 'my_func'. I did the following:

1. I copied stan/src/stan/math/functions/abs.hpp to stan/src/stan/math/functions/my_func.hpp
2. I made some mutatis mutandis changes in my_func.hpp (basically, I replaced 'abs' by 'my_func' everywhere - code
is included below).
3. I added "#include <stan/math/functions/my_func.hpp>" after line 64 (i.e., inserted this line below line 64) to stan/src/stan/math/functions.hpp
4. I added  "add_unary("my_func");" after line 586 to stan/src/stan/gm/function_signatures.h

Finally, I have written the following "model.stan" file:
"""
parameters {
  real y;
}
model {
  print(my_func(2.));
}
"""

Unfortunately, I still get the message
"""
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="my_func"
    arg 0 type=real
available function signatures for my_func :
no matches for function name="my_func"
    arg 0 type=real
available function signatures for resonances:
expression is ill formed

ERROR at line 5
  3:    }
  4:    model {
  5:      print(my_func(2.));
                              ^
  6:    }
"""
when I try to build the model. I have a feeling that I need to re-link the STAN library, but how do I do that?

N.B. I am still using STAN 2.5.0, I do not suppose that there is a difference in that issue, though.

Best regards,
Arseniy.


-----
my_func.hpp :
"""
#ifndef STAN__MATH__FUNCTIONS__MY_FUNC_HPP
#define STAN__MATH__FUNCTIONS__MY_FUNC_HPP

#include <cmath>

namespace stan {

  namespace math {

    /**
     * Return floating-point absolute value.
     *
     * Delegates to <code>fabs(double)</code> rather than
     * <code>std::abs(int)</code>.
     *
     * @param x scalar
     * @return absolute value of scalar
     */
    double my_func(double x) {
      return std::fabs(x);
    }

  }
}

#endif
"""

Hi Daniel,

I have some more troubles with user-defined functions - maybe you could help me out? I am trying to
write a function A_1 (that I will use in STAN), and this function calls another function c_one that does
some computation with Eigen matrices. I am having the following issue:

 - the function A_1 takes (and returns) some vectors with base type stan::agrad::var;
 - the function c_one takes a double and returns an instance of Eigen::Matrix<double,2,1>.

I am having conversion troubles in between - see the example below.

Here is my MWE:
File containing the function "c_one" (the file is called "c_func.hpp"):
"""
#include <stan/math/matrix/Eigen.hpp>
#include <vector>
namespace c_func
{
    using Eigen::Matrix;
    using std::vector;

    /**
     * vector c_one(scalar)
     *
     * Complex number 1.
     * Takes a (dummy) double and returns the vector (1., 0.).
     */
    inline
    Eigen::Matrix<double,2,1>
        c_one(const double& y) {
        Eigen::Matrix<double,2,1>  res;
        res(0,0) = 1.0;
        res(1,0) = 0.0;
        return res;
    }
    }
}
"""


File containing the function "A_1" (called 'model.hpp'):
"""
#include <stan/math/matrix/Eigen.hpp>
#include <boost/math/tools/promotion.hpp>
#include <vector>
#include "c_func.hpp"

namespace stan {
  namespace math {
   
    using Eigen::Matrix;
    using std::vector;

    /**
     * vector A_1(vector)
     *
     * Takes a vector y as an argument, and returns c_one(y(0,0)),
     * i.e. the result is c_one evaluated at the first element of y.
     *
     * @tparam T0__ - Scalar type of the input vector
     */
    template <typename T0__>
    inline
    Eigen::Matrix<typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<T0__>::type, Eigen::Dynamic,1>
    A_1(const Eigen::Matrix<T0__, Eigen::Dynamic,1>& y) {

        typedef typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<T0__>::type fun_scalar_t__;
        typedef fun_scalar_t__ fun_return_scalar_t__;

        Eigen::Matrix<typename boost::math::tools::promote_args<T0__>::type, Eigen::Dynamic,1> res;
        res = stan::math::promote_scalar<fun_return_scalar_t__>(c_func::c_one(y(0,0).val()));

        return res;
    }
  }
}
"""

Here is the relevant part of the error message:
"""
stan/src/../../meson_deca/lib/c_lib/model.hpp:29:85: error: member reference
      base type 'const double' is not a structure or union
  ...y(0,0).val()));
     ~~~~~~^~~~
"""
However, if I remove '.val()', I get another error, since I am calling 'c_one' with argument
of the wrong type. I have poked around here and there, but I still can not force it to work.
Any ideas?

Thanks in advance,
Regards,
Arseniy.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Contributing New Functions to Stan / Expose Function Signature to Stan Models
parts:
HI Arseniy,

Your c_one function needs to be templated to allow for an arbitrary scalar type. So:
1. prefix your function with 'template <typename T>'
2. replace 'double' with 'T'
3. Replace y(0,0).val() with y(0,0)

That should get you further. I think you'll still have problems with the Eigen rows and columns, though.


Daniel

On Friday, February 20, 2015 at 8:35:50 PM UTC+1, Daniel Lee wrote:
HI Arseniy,

Your c_one function needs to be templated to allow for an arbitrary scalar type. So:
1. prefix your function with 'template <typename T>'
2. replace 'double' with 'T'
3. Replace y(0,0).val() with y(0,0)

That should get you further. I think you'll still have problems with the Eigen rows and columns, though.


Daniel

work around that extensively in Stan. All of
the Stan functions accept mixed type inputs, but nothing
in straight-up Boost does.

- Bob
